topic_candidates.title: The Worst Week in AI Security... So Far
topic_candidates.query: FBI North Korean fake job interviews remote IT workers cybersecurity 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Start with the unsettling idea that a cyberattack can begin as an ordinary job interview. Explain how fake applicants, remote-access tools and company-issued laptops can let an attacker enter through the hiring process rather than by breaking through a firewall. Then connect it to automated attacks: once software can search for exposed systems and exploit repeatable weaknesses, one compromised account can scale much faster than a human hacker.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: The FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center warns that North Korean IT workers use fake job postings and may ask people to interview on their behalf or receive and host laptops at home. The evidence supports a workplace-infiltration story without relying on rumours about a specific unreleased attack. ([ic3.gov](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2026/PSA261013?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 2026 — cybersecurity coverage is clustering around automated attacks, fake workers and large-scale theft.
topic_candidates.science_angle: The engineering weakness is identity and trust, not just code. Attackers exploit authentication, remote management software, permissions and the assumption that a person who passed hiring checks is legitimate.

topic_candidates.title: Big Tech’s $3T AI Debt, Claude Writes 90% of Anthropic’s Code, AIs Editing AI Brains | EP #308
topic_candidates.query: Big Tech 3 trillion off balance sheet AI commitments Morgan Stanley 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Translate the AI boom into a household analogy: companies are not only buying chips and data centers today; they are signing enormous future contracts for leases, power and computing capacity. Explain why that can look smaller in headline capital-spending numbers, why the bills still have to be paid, and what happens if AI revenue grows slower than expected. Keep the focus on electricity, prices, jobs and financial risk rather than stock-picking.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Axios reported that Morgan Stanley estimated more than $3.1 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI infrastructure commitments across major technology companies, in addition to hundreds of billions in debt and leases already recorded. The figure is a commitment estimate, not proof that companies have already spent $3 trillion or are insolvent. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/27/ai-spending-spending-balance-sheet?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 3–5, 2026 — renewed attention on Big Tech borrowing and the financial cost of the AI buildout.
topic_candidates.science_angle: AI inference requires dense GPU clusters, networking, cooling and continuous electricity. The physical infrastructure behaves more like a utility-scale industrial project than a normal software update, with large fixed costs that need high utilization.

topic_candidates.title: No AI, No Choice
topic_candidates.query: Google turns off Search for schools that reject AI November 2026 AP
topic_candidates.brief: Explain the apparent contradiction: a school can reject generative AI, but Google says it may also lose access to Search. Walk through why modern search increasingly includes generated summaries, ranking systems and interactive tutoring, then ask whether an AI-free internet product is still technically possible when the same company controls the search engine, browser account and school administration tools.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: The Associated Press reported that Google will cut off Search access for students at schools that reject its AI tools. The story is not that every school is being forced to use AI immediately; it is that Google’s stated choice may be between enabling the AI features or disabling Search for student accounts. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/7ba4219e505db1c11d672f6eefe7155a?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 4, 2026 — Google’s school-account policy triggered debate over whether Search can still exist separately from AI.
topic_candidates.science_angle: Search is now a layered information-retrieval system: crawling and indexing are combined with ranking, language-model summarization and account-level policy controls. Separating those layers is partly a product decision and partly an engineering problem.
